headline: Planning a Custom Tile Shower: A Guide to Design, Slopes, and Waterproofing
articleBody:
A custom tile shower turns an ordinary bathroom into a luxury retreat, but its beauty relies entirely on what sits underneath the tile. Understanding the build process helps you hire with confidence.

Overview and Key Benefits
Custom showers allow you to tailor every detail, from built-in niches and benches to curb heights and tile patterns. Beyond aesthetics, a professionally built shower delivers a watertight assembly designed to protect your home's framing for decades.

Process Breakdown
The build begins with framing inspection and drain placement. The floor pan is prepared with a pre-slope of roughly one-quarter inch per foot toward the drain. Approved waterproof backer boards and bonded membranes are applied across walls, curbs, and niches. After critical leak and flood testing, your tile is set, grouted, sealed, and fitted with movement joints.

What to Expect During the Process
Expect proper curing times between waterproofing, tile setting, and grouting. Tile and grout alone do not block water; your underlying bonded membrane provides the real water barrier.
